column1: # NINE BORN. EIGHT LIVING IN 1911. ONE DIED. THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES EXACTLY.
# WHY THE MOTHER'S-MAIDEN-NAME SEARCH FOUND ONLY SIX, and it is three different failures:
#   SARAH ANN is indexed under WALLIS, not Castle - she is not a Castle birth at all in the index
#   MARTHA MAUD's entry carries NO mother's maiden name; the field is blank
#   SIDNEY CHARLES likewise never came back on that search
# A filter on a field that is sometimes empty is a filter on the indexing, not on the family.
# AND THE HOUSEHOLD ITSELF, read the same afternoon:
# 1901 census, RG13 piece 1298 folio 49 page 26 schedule 192, NORTON END, NORTON, BALDOCK:
#   George W Castle   Head      36   Labourer farm   b. Baldock
#   Caroline Castle   Wife      36                   b. WESTON
#   George W Castle   Son       16   Labourer farm
#   Ada Castle        Daughter  14
#   Frederick Castle  Son       11
#   Agnes K Castle    Daughter   9
#   Martha Castle     Daughter   5
# THEY HAD GONE BACK TO NORTON END - the hamlet where George William himself was raised by his
# GIDDINS grandparents in 1871 and 1881, after his mother died. He brought his own family home to it.
# A WARNING THAT BELONGS WITH THIS PAGE: three schedules away, at RG13/1298 folio 48 page 23
# schedule 175, THE SAME HAMLET HOLDS A SECOND CASTLE FAMILY - head JAMES CASTLE, 38, wife ANNIE,
# ten in the house, WITH ITS OWN FRED, aged 13. Two unrelated Castle households at Norton End on
# one census night, each with a Frederick.
# ——— ADDED 20 SEPTEMBER 2026: PROBATE, WHICH IS PRIORITY 7 OF THE FINDMYPAST ROW ———
# The second child, GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLE the younger, has been carried here on a date taken from
# A MATCH HOLDER'S USER TREE — "abt 1885 Baldock, d. 23 Aug 1939" — with no record behind it.
# The government probate index has him, and it agrees to the day.

column5: *** 23 AUGUST 1939, and it is now a record ***
column6: England & Wales Government Probate Death Index 1858-2019, record GBOR/GOVPROBATE/C/1939-1939/00022564. DEATH DATE 23 AUG 1939 · RESIDENCE TOWN LETCHWORTH, HERTFORDSHIRE · PROBATE GRANTED 2 NOVEMBER 1939 AT THE LONDON REGISTRY · LINKED PERSON: CYRIL GEORGE CASTLE. The date the match holder's tree gave is confirmed to the day by a government index, which is the whole point of checking.

column1: 2a — AND HE WAS IN LETCHWORTH
column6: THE SAME TOWN AS THE WEARS. Martha Maud, his sister, was at 72 Pix Road, Letchworth; her youngest brother Ernest Albert Cyril Castle was at 9 Boscombe Place, Letchworth in the 1921 census. The Castles had moved from Baldock to Letchworth and the Wears went to the same place. This is a plain fact about where two families lived and it is not offered as a reason for anything.

column1: 2b — AND THE DATES SIT THIRTEEN DAYS APART
column6: MARTHA MAUD WEAR SAILED FROM LONDON ON THE DUNVEGAN CASTLE ON 10 AUGUST 1939 with the four youngest children, bound for Durban. HER BROTHER DIED ON 23 AUGUST 1939 — AT ST BARTHOLOMEW'S HOSPITAL IN LONDON, not at Letchworth, which the calendar page below corrects and which this row had wrong. She had been gone a fortnight. Both halves are documented — BT27 on one side, the probate index on the other.

column1: 2c — A NAME THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT HAVE
column6: *** CYRIL GEORGE CASTLE ***, the linked person on the probate entry, which in this index is the executor or next of kin. He is NOT the ninth child, who is Ernest Albert Cyril Castle of Baldock (1903-1988) — the forenames are in a different order and the surname order is fixed. The likeliest reading is a SON of the deceased. NOT ASSERTED, and he is a new Castle to chase.

column1: 2d — WHAT WAS NOT READ, AND WHY
column6: the original probate calendar page would give the STREET ADDRESS, the OCCUPATION, the EXECUTORS BY NAME and the VALUE OF THE ESTATE. It is served as IIIF at 2864 x 4361 pixels behind Findmypast's image gateway, and the gateway is SESSION-LOCKED: a request carrying the visible cookies returns 403. The page is at record id GBOR/GOVPROBATE/1939/C000740-CASSON-1939 for whoever opens it next inside a signed-in browser.

column1: # ---------------- 12 OCTOBER 2026: THE CALENDAR PAGE IS READ, AND 2d IS CLOSED ----------------
2e — THE ENTRY IN FULL, TRANSCRIBED FROM THE IMAGE
column6: CASTLE George William of 85 JACKMANS-PLACE LETCHWORTH Hertfordshire died 23 August 1939 at ST. BARTHOLOMEWS HOSPITAL LONDON E.C.1 ADMINISTRATION London 2 November to MARGARET CASTLE WIDOW and CYRIL GEORGE CASTLE PRINTER. Effects £1166 13s. 2d. Read at the image 12 October 2026 in a signed-in session, in four overlapping IIIF regions at native resolution so that no figure rests on a downscaled view.

column1: 2f — AND IT CORRECTS THIS FILE: HE DID NOT DIE AT LETCHWORTH
column6: *** HE DIED IN A LONDON HOSPITAL. *** Letchworth is his RESIDENCE, which is the only thing the index gave and which row 2b read as the place of death. ST BARTHOLOMEW'S, LONDON E.C.1, is forty miles from Jackmans-place. THE THIRTEEN-DAY READING IS UNHARMED and is slightly sharpened: his sister sailed FROM LONDON on 10 August and he died IN LONDON on the 23rd.

column1: 2g — ADMINISTRATION, NOT PROBATE, WHICH IS A FACT ABOUT HIM
column6: the word on the page is ADMINISTRATION. A grant of administration rather than probate means THERE WAS NO WILL — he died intestate at about fifty-four. The index's own column had called it probate and this archive repeated it.

column1: 2h — AND IT NAMES HIS WIDOW, WHICH THE INDEX DID NOT
column6: *** MARGARET CASTLE, WIDOW. *** A wife this archive has never held under any spelling. She takes the administration jointly with CYRIL GEORGE CASTLE, PRINTER — who now has an OCCUPATION and is a co-administrator with the widow, which is the position a SON ordinarily occupies. STILL NOT ASSERTED: a co-administrator is not a proven relationship, and no document here says he is her son.

column1: 2i — THE ESTATE
column6: EFFECTS £1166 13s. 2d. Read at native resolution and worth saying why: a downscaled view of the same line read as "£1100 15s. 2d." and would have been written down wrong. The figures are the first thing to go.

column1: 2j — THE TRAP ON THE SAME PAGE, RECORDED SO NOBODY TAKES THE WRONG MAN
column6: *** THERE ARE TWO GEORGE WILLIAM CASTLES IN THE 1939 CALENDAR, TWENTY LINES APART. *** The other is "of 3 CISSBURY-ROAD WORTHING ... probate London 4 August to DOROTHY KATE CAST[LE] ... £2466 12s. 3d." — Sussex, probate not administration, a different grant date and nearly twice the estate. Only the RESIDENCE TOWN separates them in the index.

column1: 2k — THE ROUTE, FOR WHOEVER OPENS THE NEXT ONE
column6: the gateway is session-locked and the 403 reported in 2d was real, but the image IS reachable from inside a signed-in browser. THE URL FORM NEEDS BOTH IDS: search.findmypast.com.au/record?id=<IMAGE id>&parentid=<TRANSCRIPT id> — the image id alone returns 500 and /transcript? with the image id returns 404. From there the IIIF service is /titan/marshal/record-gateway/image/<image id>/info.json with parentRecordId and recordMetadataId, level 2, regionByPx, so a line can be pulled at native resolution instead of squinting at the viewer.
